papers.title_en: Fast Bayesian Inference for Long-Duration Gravitational-Wave Signals in 3G detectors
papers.evidence: 以JKS分解和相对分箱加速长时引力波信号贝叶斯推断，与贝叶斯模型高效采样相关
papers.tldr: 第三代引力波探测器将观测持续近一天的双中子星旋进信号，地球自转调制使信号无法再分解为独立的内在和外在参数，导致贝叶斯推断计算成本急剧上升。本文证明，采用JKS五谐波分解能够精确分离旋转天线波束响应与昂贵的固有波形计算，并在此基础上对按相位曲率选取的频率网格使用误差可控的相对分箱方法，使21.3小时信号的似然评估加速约四个数量级。这一方案让持续整日的第三代探测器引力波信号的快速贝叶斯推断成为现实。
papers.abstract_en: Third-generation (3G) gravitational-wave detectors will observe binary-neutron-star inspirals for nearly a day, so Earth's rotation becomes part of the signal rather than a negligible correction. This destroys the usual separation between intrinsic and extrinsic parameters and creates a major computational bottleneck for Bayesian inference. We show that the exact five-harmonic Jaranowski-Krolak-Schutz (JKS) decomposition restores the separation of the rotating antenna amplitude response from the computationally expensive intrinsic waveform calculations. By sampling the intrinsic waveform on a frequency grid set by its phase curvature and then applying error-controlled relative binning, likelihood evaluations for a 21.3-h signal are accelerated by O(10^4), making day-long 3G signal inference practical.
